steps.title: Prepare complete medium
steps.instruction: Thaw HI FBS and L‑Glutamine at 37 °C for 1 h (or at 4 °C overnight). Remove 55 mL DMEM from a fresh bottle, split into two 50 mL conical tubes, add 50 mL HI FBS (10 %) and 5 mL L‑Glutamine (1 %). Mix to a final volume of 500 mL (445 mL DMEM, 50 mL FBS, 5 mL L‑Glutamine). Store at 4 °C. All steps in a Class II biosafety cabinet.

steps.title: Prepare complete medium with G418
steps.instruction: Follow the complete medium recipe, but remove 62 mL DMEM and add 7 mL G418 (700 µg/mL). Final composition: 438 mL DMEM, 50 mL HI FBS, 5 mL L‑Glutamine, 7 mL G418, total 500 mL. Store at 4 °C. All steps in a Class II biosafety cabinet.

steps.title: Make 1× PBS
steps.instruction: Dissolve one PBS tablet in 100 mL de‑ionised water. Prepare two bottles: one for cell culture (autoclave) and one for general lab work (autoclave optional). Store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare Hoechst 33342 stock
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 mg Hoechst 33342, dissolve in 1 mL dH₂O, vortex, centrifuge 140 × g for 1 min. Aliquot 50 µL portions, store at –20 °C protected from light. Stable ≥1 year.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M glycine solution
steps.instruction: Weigh 3.753 g glycine, add 50 mL PBS (Recipe 3), vortex to dissolve. Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 30 mM glycine solution
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 mL of the 1 M glycine stock to 48.5 mL PBS (Recipe 3). Vortex to mix. Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 10 % Triton X‑100
steps.instruction: Slowly add 5 mL Triton X‑100 to 45 mL PBS (Recipe 3), vortex until homogeneous. Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 0.5 % Triton X‑100
steps.instruction: Mix 2.5 mL of the 10 % Triton X‑100 solution with 47.5 mL PBS (Recipe 3). Vortex to homogenise. Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 10 % sodium azide solution
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, weigh 1 g sodium azide, add 10 mL dH₂O, vortex until dissolved. Store in a well‑ventilated place. (Caution: toxic)

steps.title: Prepare BFA stock solution
steps.instruction: Add 5 mg BFA to 500 µL DMSO (10 mg/mL). Vortex to dissolve, aliquot 50 µL, store at –20 °C. Perform in a Class II biosafety cabinet.

steps.title: Prepare nocodazole stock solution
steps.instruction: Add 2 mg nocodazole to 660 µL DMSO (10 mM). Vortex to dissolve, aliquot 50 µL, store at –20 °C. Perform in a Class II biosafety cabinet.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M calcium chloride
steps.instruction: Weigh 1.47 g calcium chloride dihydrate, add 10 mL PBS (Recipe 3), vortex to dissolve. Store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M magnesium chloride
steps.instruction: Weigh 2.03 g magnesium chloride hexahydrate, add 10 mL PBS (Recipe 3), vortex to dissolve. Store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 3 % PFA solution
steps.instruction: Heat 400 mL autoclaved PBS to 60–70 °C while stirring. Turn off hood, weigh 15 g PFA, add to PBS, keep at 60–70 °C until dissolved (add a few drops of 5 M NaOH if needed). Add 50 µL 1 M calcium chloride and 50 µL 1 M magnesium chloride, adjust volume to 500 mL with PBS, adjust pH to 7.4 with NaOH or HCl, filter through Stericup, aliquot, store at –20 °C (stable ≥1 year). Wear mask and gloves; PFA toxic.

steps.title: Warm CYTOO plate
steps.instruction: Remove CYTOO plate from the fridge, place in the Class II biosafety cabinet at room temperature for 1 h.

steps.title: Prime plate with medium
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL complete medium (Recipe 1) to each well of the warmed CYTOO plate.

steps.title: Incubate plate before seeding
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a humidified incubator at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for at least 10 min. The plate is then ready for cell plating.

steps.title: Prepare cells for plating
steps.instruction: Warm complete medium and 0.05 % trypsin‑EDTA to 37 °C. When HeLa Kyoto cells reach ~80 % confluence in a 10 cm dish (~4 × 10⁶ cells in 12 mL medium), wash with 2 mL 1× PBS, aspirate, add 3 mL 0.05 % trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 3–4 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Add 7 mL complete medium, wash the dish to detach remaining cells, collect the total 10 mL suspension into a 50 mL conical tube and pipette up/down for homogeneity.

steps.title: Count cells
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL of the suspension to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube. Count cells using a Scepter 2.0 with the 60 µm sensor (or a hemocytometer). Multiply the counted number by 10 to obtain the total cell number in the original suspension.

steps.title: Adjust cell concentration
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cell suspension at 135 × g for 4 min at room temperature. Aspirate supernatant, resuspend the pellet in complete medium to achieve 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL.

steps.title: Make plating suspension
steps.instruction: For each well, mix 5 µL of the 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL suspension with 95 µL complete medium to obtain 5,000 cells in 100 µL. Prepare enough volume for all wells plus 5 extra wells (or +10 % if using a Multidrop). Keep the tube in the Class II cabinet until plating.

steps.title: Plate cells onto CYTOO plate
steps.instruction: Gently pipette the cell suspension up/down to maintain homogeneity, then add 100 µL of this suspension to each well that already contains 100 µL complete medium (step B). Use an electronic 8‑channel pipette at the slowest speed, placing the tip over the centre of the well and releasing slowly. Automated dispensers (e.g., Multidrop) may be used.

steps.title: Grow spheroids
steps.instruction: Incubate the seeded plate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Allow spheroids to develop for 3 days, monitoring with a light microscope. Check initial adhesion after ~1 h. Perform a medium exchange the next day by removing 150 µL of medium and adding 150 µL fresh complete medium; repeat 2–3 times. For longer cultures, exchange medium every 2 days.

steps.title: Immunostaining – remove medium
steps.instruction: Using an electronic 8‑channel pipette at the slowest speed, aspirate all medium from each well. Keep the plate covered with aluminium foil throughout staining.

steps.title: Fix spheroids
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL 3 % PFA (Recipe 14) to each well, incubate 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Quench fixation
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL 30 mM glycine in PBS (Recipe 6) to each well, incubate 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash after quench
steps.instruction: Wash spheroids twice with 1× PBS (Recipe 3).

steps.title: Pause point after wash
steps.instruction: If needed, store the plate at 4 °C (still covered with foil) for up to a few days before continuing.

steps.title: Permeabilise spheroids
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL 0.5 % Triton X‑100 (Recipe 8) to each well, incubate 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash after permeabilisation
steps.instruction: Wash spheroids twice with 1× PBS.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare primary antibody solution in PBS containing 0.02 % sodium azide (Recipe 9). Use rabbit anti‑GM130 1:500, mouse anti‑EEA1 1:200, and mouse anti‑LAMP1 1:200 (adjust per antibody). Add 100 µL to each well, incubate 2 h at room temperature (or overnight at RT or 4 °C).

steps.title: Wash after primary
steps.instruction: Wash spheroids twice with 1× PBS.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare secondary antibody solution in PBS containing 0.2 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 (stock from Recipe 4) and 0.02 % sodium azide. Use goat anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 1:400 and goat anti‑mouse Alexa Fluor 647 1:400. Add 100 µL to each well, incubate 2 h at room temperature (or overnight at RT or 4 °C).

steps.title: Final washes
steps.instruction: Wash spheroids twice with 1× PBS.

steps.title: Store stained plates
steps.instruction: Cover the plate with aluminium foil and store at 4 °C. Image the spheroids within 2 weeks for optimal fluorescence.

steps.title: Prepare drug solutions
steps.instruction: Freshly dilute BFA stock (10 mg/mL) to 10 µg/mL and nocodazole stock (10 mM) to 7.5 µM in pre‑warmed complete medium (37 °C).

steps.title: Drug treatment of spheroids
steps.instruction: Remove existing medium from each well, add 100 µL of the appropriate drug solution (BFA or nocodazole). Incubate 30 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Post‑drug fixation and staining
steps.instruction: Proceed with the fixation and immunofluorescence steps described in section C (steps 1–11).

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in the following research article: • Mysior and Simpson [22]. An automated high-content screening and assay platform for the analysis of spheroids at subcellular resolution. PLoS One , 19(11), e0311963. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0311963 In the supplementary information in this article, readers will also find seven supplementary tables detailing, step-by-step, seven different image analysis pipelines. These use the commercial imaging analysis software Harmony that is provided with Opera Phenix microscope. In general, approximately 90% of micropatterns were occupied by cells shortly after seeding. After 3 days of growth, approximately 60%–80% of the micropatterns contained spheroids [22]. At this point, using a pre-scan function on the microscope, spheroids with particular size characteristics can be selected for higher resolution imaging. Using this approach, primary characterisation of the spheroids showed that each had a similar average area, and that this was also consistent between the different cell lines (see Figure 1C in [22]). Furthermore, the average spheroid volume (Figure 2B in [22]) and the number of nuclei per spheroid (Figure 2D in [22]) were in the same range for all cell lines. The overexpression of some proteins, particularly those that play a role in cell division or assembly of the plasma membrane, can result in changes to spheroid size and other properties. For example, we found that spheroids overexpressing EGFP-Rab6A were on average 20% smaller than the other spheroids (Figure 2A, D in [22]). However, a key advantage of this method is that several hundred spheroids can be generated per well, compared to more commonly used methods such as U-bottomed ULA plates and hanging drop methods, which typically produce only one spheroid per well or drop.
